about: Reference values for flowsheet-validation.html, computed OUTSIDE the engine. pr: Caleb Bell thermo 0.6.1 (FlashVL with PRMIX gas/liquid phases, Gibbs-stability flash) using the engine's own Tc/Pc/omega, the H2 effective constants (Tc 43.6 K, Pc 20.5 bar, omega 0) and the eos.js kij table — an implementation check of the phi-phi flash. nrtl: thermo.nrtl.NRTL activity coefficients at the stated liquid composition. wetgas: CoolProp 8.0 (IAPWS-95 water, reference EOS for N2/CO2) at component partial pressures with a Raoult split at 40 °C / 4.8 bar. Regenerate with the Python scripts kept alongside the Step-21 build if any input changes. dwsim: DWSIM 9.0.5 (Linux build, Peng-Robinson (PR) property package, default flash, run through its .NET automation API) on the same feeds. same_data = DWSIM given the engine's Tc/Pc/omega, H2 effective constants and kij (a second implementation check); dwsim_data = DWSIM with its own built-in constants and kij (shows how much the answer depends on input data).

wetgas.desc: 20 mol % steam in N2/CO2 at 150 °C / 5 bar + N2 at 25 °C → cooler 40 °C → knock-out 4.8 bar

step22.about: Step 22 references (rigorous property packages). columns: DWSIM 9.0.5 rigorous distillation column (Naphtali–Sandholm), same ChemSep data, Poynting and Henry off — condenser/reboiler duty kW, product compositions, stage temperatures. three_phase: Caleb Bell thermo 0.6.1 FlashVLN (PR gas + two PR liquids) and isoactivity LLE solved with scipy using thermo NRTL / UNIFAC / Dortmund-UNIFAC gammas. janaf: NIST-JANAF ΔfG° at 1000 K. flashes: DWSIM 9.0.5 flashes are stored in tests/mb-vectors.json (MB-118…MB-142). The test vectors MB-104…MB-142 carry these values as expectations.

step23.about: Step 23 references. envelope: DWSIM 9.0.5 phase envelopes (same ChemSep constants and kij) — critical points by Heidemann–Khalil and the maximum dew temperature of DWSIM's dew curve. property_table: thermo 0.6.1 PRMIX gas root (density, Z). binary: modified Raoult's law with thermo 0.6.1 NRTL / UNIFAC activity coefficients and the ChemSep vapour-pressure equations, solved with scipy (azeotropes by brentq on y1 − x1, heteroazeotropes from isoactivity LLE + bubble condition). kinetics: Levenspiel closed forms (K1, K2), scipy LSODA / brentq on the ideal-gas balances with the ChemSep Cp (K3–K6, incl. all three steady states of K5), closed-form eigen-solution of a stiff linear system, NIST-JANAF water-gas-shift equilibrium. gibbs: NIST-JANAF ΔfG° of NH3. The test vectors MB-143…MB-164 carry these values as expectations.

step24.about: Step 24 references. lhhw: closed-form Langmuir–Hinshelwood PFR/CSTR solutions (L1, L2) and scipy LSODA solutions of the published Xu & Froment (1989) steam-reforming kinetics, isothermal (X1) and adiabatic with ChemSep ideal-gas Cp (X2), rate constants × 0.03. association: independent chemical-theory implementation (scipy least-squares on true-species amounts) with K_D(acetic) = exp(−17.374 + 7290/T) bar⁻¹ (DECHEMA) and log10 K_D(propionic) = −10.834 + 3316/T mmHg⁻¹; nist_liquid_dHf_kJmol: NIST WebBook liquid enthalpies of formation. The test vectors MB-165…MB-174 carry these values as expectations.

step25.about: Step 25 references: acid-gas electrolyte packages (aqueous MEA, hot potassium carbonate) and Murphree tray efficiencies. All values come from outside the engine.

idaes_dh_abs.source: IDAES MEA property package, dh_abs_co2 = −84 kJ/mol (heat of absorption of CO2 in aqueous MEA)

arshad2014.source: Arshad, Fosbøl, von Solms, Svendsen, Thomsen, J. Chem. Eng. Data 59 (2014) 764 — NIST ThermoML 10.1021/je400886w; 30 wt % MEA (7.017 mol/kg water)

phreeqc_grid.source: USGS PHREEQC 3 (IPhreeqc via phreeqpython 1.x) with pitzer.dat; 1 kg water + K2CO3 + CO2 as a REACTION at 1 atm (PHREEQC raises P to the water vapour pressure above 100 °C)

armand.source: Armand Products, Potassium Carbonate Handbook — Table 4 (density, 15.6 °C), Table 5 (specific gravity vs temperature), Table 7 (heat capacity, 21–52 °C), Table 12 (water vapour pressure at 20.5 °C)

step27.source: N. Sadegh, PhD thesis, Technical University of Denmark (2013), Tables 7-13 to 7-17: CO2 solubility in aqueous MDEA at 110 kPa total pressure — measured loading (volumetric method, this thesis) and the loading calculated by the thesis's Extended UNIQUAC model. Rows [MDEA wt %, measured loading, thesis-model loading] by temperature (°C). The thesis states 7–10 % uncertainty for 10 wt % and 8–10 % at 80 °C, 2 % otherwise, and model AARDs of 15, 21, 21, 29 and 32 % against these measurements.

step28.source: Measured CO2 partial pressures over MDEA/piperazine and aqueous piperazine: Chen X. (2011) PhD thesis, University of Texas at Austin, Tables 4.7-4.8 (wetted-wall column, 7 m MDEA/2 m PZ and 5 m MDEA/5 m PZ, 40-100 C); Xu Q. (2011) PhD thesis, University of Texas at Austin, Tables 2-2, 2-8, 2-9 (total-pressure cell, 100-160 C; P(CO2) = measured total pressure minus water and amine) and Table 2-10 (empirical correlation for aqueous PZ regressed to Hilliard 2008, Dugas 2008, Ermatchkov 2006, Nguyen 2010, Kamps 2003). Densities: Frailie P. (2014) PhD thesis, University of Texas at Austin, Table C-1.
step28.loading_basis: mol CO2 per mol alkalinity (MDEA + 2 PZ)
step28.fit: piperazine parameters regressed to chen72, xu72, xu55, xupz and pzcorr; chen55 held out

pr_rig.about: STEP 32: the six Peng–Robinson cases of 'pr' re-run for the DEFAULT rigorous path (r-flash, property method Peng–Robinson): Caleb Bell thermo 0.6.1 FlashVL with PRMIX gas/liquid phases given the engine's ChemSep critical constants (true H2 constants 33.19 K / 13.13 bar / -0.216) and the engine's k_ij matrix as stored here; the less dense phase is reported as vapour (the engine's convention).

step32.about: STEP 32 references, computed OUTSIDE the engine: water and steam with CoolProp 8.0.0 (IAPWS-95, HEOS backend); Henry constants of gases in water from IAPWS G7-04 via the iapws Python package 1.5.5 (kH in MPa).

W1.desc: 1,000 kg/h water heated from 25 °C to 200 °C at 10 bar (superheated steam out)

W2.desc: 1,000 kg/h water at 25 °C, 10 bar with 500 kW added

W3.desc: 1,000 kg/h saturated steam condensed to saturated liquid at 4 bar

W4.desc: 1,000 kg/h saturated steam condensed to saturated liquid at 100 bar

W5.desc: superheated steam 400 °C / 40 bar let down to 10 bar

W6.desc: 1,000 kg/h water pumped from 1 bar to 100 bar at 30 °C, efficiency 0.75

W7.desc: water over liquid water in N₂ at 40 °C, 1.013 bar (reference: IAPWS-95 saturation pressure; the real gas-phase enhancement at 1 bar is about +0.4 %)
